---
applyTo: "{packages/react-transfer/**,packages/react/runtime/src/internal.ts,packages/react/runtime/src/snapshot/independent/**,packages/react/runtime/__test__/snapshot/lifecycle/independent*.test.jsx,examples/react/src/transfer-chat.tsx,examples/react/TRANSFER_CHAT.md}"
---

Keep transfer registration, ContextProxy event names, instance generations, props versions and commit ACK queues in `@lynx-js/react-transfer`. ReactLynx owns snapshot root wrappers, first-frame rendering, hydration, patch application, Preact hooks and native event handling. Add only `createMainThreadRenderer` and `createBackgroundRenderer` to the existing `@lynx-js/react/internal` entry. The main-thread renderer provides `initialize`, `createRoot` (returning `render` and `destroy`) and `applyCommit`; the background renderer provides `createRoot` (returning `render`, `hydrate` and `destroy`), `getCurrentRoot`, `flushEvents` and `dispose`. Underlying Snapshot instances, raw patch queues/managers and hook installers remain renderer implementation details. Do not introduce a separate renderer extension entry or install independent renderer hooks on ordinary pages. Use package exports and the application's shared Preact dependency, never relative imports of a second runtime source tree. Run the transfer protocol integration tests in the snapshot runtime harness so both sides exercise the same renderer and native mocks; renderer commit/event hook tests belong under `packages/react/runtime/__test__/snapshot/lifecycle/` and import runtime sources directly. Business code registers component providers and never receives a render context.

Native commands `__CreateTransfer`, `__SetTransferProps` and `__DestroyTransfer` arrive on MTS through `lynx.getNative()` on the Native ContextProxy channel, with the command object directly in event `data`; `__RenderPage` remains an Engine event. MTS/BTS protocol messages use the JS-context/core-context channels. The recorded emulator verification used the earlier Engine command route; the sibling prototype host must migrate its sender to Native before those results can validate the current listeners.

The companion package's API Extractor reads generated declarations from `lib`; its Turbo API task must depend on its own build, because CI runs API checks before a full repository build. Its TypeScript-only build depends on `//#build` rather than `^build`; the latter pulls renderer Rust/WASM builds into the API-check job, which does not install Cargo. Declare `lib/**` as build outputs so downstream CI jobs restore the package's JavaScript and declarations on Turbo cache hits; a successful cached task without those files breaks package resolution.
